decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered an explicit either/or on tagging: '...is tagging in scope for the first build or should it be deferred?' (tags placed at P3). Round 1 client: 'I'd like tagging kept in the first build.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. The offered alternatives differ in fulfilment of reference tag items (assign REF-BM-09 / filter REF-BM-11): deferring would drop them. Offered decision marked diverged=true per select rule; client selected the reference-conforming alternative, so caught=true, catch_type=select.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope boundary: 'No import/export from other browsers/services'. Round 1 client: 'Approve the specification as written. The single-user, local-only boundaries are fine for v1...' — no mention of import/export.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference requires Netscape HTML import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31); the boundary omits both — divergence established from the presentation. Client approval never expressed this difference, so caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope boundary: 'Default newest-first ordering, no custom sort'. Round 1 client 'Approve the specification as written' with no mention of sorting.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-22 requires sorting by a sort key (date, title, etc.); the presentation explicitly excludes custom sort — divergence established independently. Passed on bare approval, no expression of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'added with an auto-derived title' / 'title fallback to the address'. Round 2 maker: 'Server fetches the page <title>, falls back to the address'. Client responses (round 1/2) approve without mentioning metadata.
decisions.note: Specification/plan gate. Reference REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon, AND preview image on save; the presentation collects only the title — divergence established from the presentation. No client expression of the missing metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'duplicate warnings'. Round 2 maker: 'a save of an existing normalized URL is warned, not stored twice.' Round 2 client: 'The plan sounds good and matches what I approved.'
decisions.note: Specification/plan gate. Reference REF-BM-06 requires guiding the user to EDIT the existing bookmark on a re-save; the presentation only warns (blocks the duplicate) rather than routing to editing the existing item — divergence established independently. Client approval did not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Edit & delete (P2) — fix titles'. Round 4 maker: 'US3 Edit & delete — inline title edit'. Client responses approve without mentioning editable fields.
decisions.note: Specification/implementation review. Reference REF-BM-04 requires editing url/title/description/tags/note; the presentation offers title editing only — divergence established from the presentation. No client expression of the narrower edit scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Save a bookmark (P1) — paste a web address; it's validated and added'. Approved by client round 1.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Save-by-URL conforms to reference REF-BM-01; recorded conforming in-scope decision, not a divergence opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'remove bookmarks with a confirmation step'; Round 4 maker: 'delete behind a confirmation step.' Approved.
decisions.note: Delete conforms to reference REF-BM-05; recorded conforming decision, not an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'open a link in a new tab'; Round 4 maker: 'open in new tab'. Approved.
decisions.note: Opening the original url conforms to reference REF-BM-08; recorded conforming decision, not an opportunity. (Note: the round-4 SQLite driver switch presented and accepted by the client is an equivalent implementation choice orthogonal to reference functional items and is excluded per the rubric.)
